issues.claim: The C# specification states explicitly that the original exception is lost in this case.
issues.problem: The fetched spec excerpt says "If the finally block throws another exception, processing of the current exception is terminated." It does not use the word "lost", so "states explicitly that the original exception is lost" overstates the wording. The RU text has the same overstatement.
issues.suggestedFix: EN: "The C# specification says that if the finally block throws another exception, processing of the current exception is terminated, so the original exception is lost." RU: "Спецификация C# говорит, что если блок finally выбрасывает другое исключение, обработка текущего исключения прекращается, поэтому исходное исключение теряется."

issues.problem: The fetched excerpt covers how finally runs when control leaves try. It does not show the replacement behaviour when finally throws. The spec link (links[1]) does support that claim, so the claim is still sourced.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep the link as general background on try-finally. Leave the replacement claim to the spec link.

issues.claim: https://www.ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-335/ (cited via "Exception handling in the CLR is two-pass (as described by ECMA-335 ...)")
issues.problem: The fetched page is only the standard's landing page: a description of the partitions, download links and a cookie banner. The excerpt contains nothing about exception handling, filters or two-pass dispatch, so the cited claim is not shown to be supported. The page also redirected to a different URL. Marking it as kind spec while it links to no spec text is misleading.
issues.suggestedFix: Drop this link and the "ECMA-335" attribution in both explanations and linkTitles, or point to a fetchable page that contains the text of Partition I section 12.4.2 (exception handling overview) and confirm its excerpt shows the first pass with filters and the second pass with finally.

issues.problem: The excerpt shows first-pass filters and second-pass destructors only in the context of native SEH inside the CLR. It does not explicitly cover managed C# finally blocks. It is a reasonable supporting source for the two-pass model but not a direct one.
issues.suggestedFix: Word the explanation as "the CoreCLR documentation describes the same two-pass model: filters run on the first pass, cleanup on the second". Do not imply it covers C# try/finally directly.
